Add Gene Annotations

Source: R/annotate.R
run_annotation.Rd

Adds functional annotations to a data frame containing gene symbols using pre-computed OmniPath annotations. The function supports both human and mouse gene symbols.

Usage

run_annotation(
  df,
  gene_column = "gene",
  org.from = "human",
  org.to = "mouse",
  release = "105",
  one.to.many = FALSE
)

Arguments

df

Data frame containing gene symbols

gene_column

Name of the column containing gene symbols. Default is "gene"

org.from

Organism type. Either "human" or "mouse". Default is "human"

org.to

Target organism. Either "human" or "mouse". Default is "mouse"

release

Ensembl release version to use for annotations. Default is "105"

one.to.many

Logical. Default is FALSE to return only unique mappings (one/many to one). If TRUE, returns all possible mouse gene mappings (one to many), including cases where one human gene maps to multiple mouse genes.

Value

A data frame with additional columns containing functional annotations: - Pathway information - Protein-protein interactions - Gene regulatory relationships - Other functional annotations from OmniPath
